cards.front: Causes of oligohydramnios include PROM, fetal renal [___] (Potter sequence), uteroplacental insufficiency, and post-dates pregnancy.
cards.context:
Fetal urine is the dominant source of amniotic fluid from T2 onwards — anything reducing fetal urine production or allowing fluid escape produces oligohydramnios.

Causes: PROM (fluid escape); renal agenesis (Potter sequence — no source); uteroplacental insufficiency (reduced renal perfusion); post-dates (placental decline).

cards.front: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first [___] months and continued breastfeeding with complementary foods until at least 2 years.
cards.context:
The benefit is dose-dependent: longer exclusive breastfeeding means lower infant mortality, fewer episodes of gastroenteritis and otitis media, less atopy and obesity, and better cognitive outcomes.

Mothers gain reduced breast and ovarian cancer risk.

Australian uptake falls off fast — ~60% exclusive at discharge but only ~25% by 6 months, driven by return-to-work pressure, formula marketing, and unsupported lactation.

cards.front: Normal pregnancy arterial blood gas (ABG) shows a chronic compensated respiratory alkalosis with PaCO₂ around 30 mmHg and HCO₃⁻ around [___] mmol/L.
cards.context: The driver is progesterone, which acts on the central respiratory chemoreceptors to raise tidal volume by ~40% (rate is unchanged). The kidneys then excrete bicarbonate to keep pH near the upper limit of normal.

cards.front: The 4 Ts of postpartum haemorrhage are Tone (commonest, ~70%), [___] (lacerations), Tissue (retained), and Thrombin (coagulopathy).
cards.context:
The 4 Ts mnemonic for PPH ranks causes by frequency: Tone (atony, ~70%), Trauma (~20%), Tissue (~10%), Thrombin (<1%).

Trauma — cervical/vaginal/perineal lacerations, uterine rupture → surgical repair; Tissue — retained placenta/membranes → manual removal; Thrombin — coagulopathy (DIC, anticoagulants) → correct with blood products.

cards.front: The ideal fetal presentation is flexed vertex, occiput anterior; the smallest presenting diameter is the [___] (~9.5 cm).
cards.context:
The fetal head is not a sphere — different presenting diameters depend on degree of flexion and orientation.

Deflexed heads (military, brow, face) present larger diameters (~11-13 cm) that may not fit → obstructed labour.

Occiput posterior (OP) babies present a slightly larger diameter (~10 cm) AND face the wrong way for the pelvic curve → prolonged labour + 'back labour'.

cards.front: The Safer Baby Bundle's five modifiable risk factors include [___] cessation, growth surveillance, awareness of decreased fetal movements, side-sleeping position from 28 weeks, and timing of birth at 41+0 weeks for low-risk pregnancies.
cards.context:
The Safer Baby Bundle (Stillbirth CRE) bundles five modifiable late-stillbirth levers so they get addressed together rather than piecemeal.

The five: smoking cessation, fetal growth surveillance (customised charts + acting on slowing growth), decreased fetal movement awareness, side-sleeping from 28 weeks, and birth timing at 41+0 for low-risk pregnancies.

Rollout shows ~25% reduction in stillbirth at participating sites. The point of the card is the set, since each lever alone has modest effect.

cards.front: Chorionicity in twins must be determined by [___] weeks; lambda sign indicates DCDA, T sign indicates MCDA.
cards.context:
Lambda (λ) sign = a triangular wedge of placental tissue pushing into the base of the dividing membrane → dichorionic (DCDA).

T sign = the membrane meets the placenta at a right angle with no wedge of tissue → monochorionic (MCDA). Both are reliable ONLY in the first trimester (thick membrane, visible placental insertion).

Mis-classification matters: MCDA share one placenta — 2-weekly scans from 16 weeks (TTTS 10-15%, TAPS, selective FGR); DCDA need 4-weekly from 20 weeks.

cards.front: On serial testing in a normally progressing IUP, βhCG rises appropriately; a plateau or falling level is consistent with a [___] pregnancy.
cards.context:
In pregnancy of unknown location, compare serum βhCG about 48 hours apart and repeat transvaginal ultrasound; the trend does not locate the pregnancy by itself.

A rise greater than 63% suggests a developing IUP, while a smaller rise, plateau or fall needs prompt clinical review. A viable pregnancy does not have to double in 48 hours.

No visible IUP above a locally used discriminatory level raises concern for ectopic pregnancy but does not prove it without the full clinical and imaging picture.

cards.front: Anti-D prophylaxis is given to all Rh(D)-negative women starting at 28 weeks gestation (with a second dose 6 weeks later) to prevent maternal [___] to the D antigen.
cards.context:
In Rh(D)-negative women carrying Rh(D)-positive babies, fetal red cells crossing into maternal circulation can sensitise the mother to the D antigen.

Resulting IgG anti-D crosses the placenta and attacks fetal red cells, sparing the first pregnancy but causing haemolytic disease in later D-positive pregnancies.

Prophylaxis works passively: anti-D clears fetal D-positive cells before maternal B cells meet them. Give 625 IU IM at 28 and 34 weeks (or 1500 IU single dose at 28), plus postnatal within 72 h if cord is Rh-positive.

cards.front: Diabetes first arising in pregnancy, screened with an oral glucose tolerance test, is [___] diabetes.
cards.context:
Glucose intolerance first recognised in pregnancy, screened around 24–28 weeks with an oral glucose tolerance test.

It drives macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and shoulder dystocia, and flags future maternal type 2 risk.

cards.front: The cardinal movements of labour in order are engagement, descent, [___], internal rotation, extension, restitution, and external rotation.
cards.context:
The cardinal movements describe how the fetal head and body navigate the pelvis during vaginal delivery.

In order: engagement → descent → flexion → internal rotation → extension → restitution → external rotation → expulsion.

The head presents a smaller diameter by flexing, rotates internally to fit the AP pelvic diameter, then extends under the symphysis pubis to deliver.

cards.front: Male factor contributes to about [___]% of infertile couples; diagnosis requires two abnormal semen analyses.
cards.context:
Male factor is the sole or contributing cause in roughly 50% of infertility cases. Testing the woman first and the man only if 'nothing comes up' misses half the diagnoses and delays treatment.

Standard practice is parallel workup: female cycle history + day 2-5 hormones + ovulation confirmation + tubal patency, alongside male history + semen analysis from the start.

Two semen samples are required before diagnosing male factor because count, motility, and morphology fluctuate substantially day-to-day from illness, fever, abstinence period, and stress.

cards.front: Under the 2025 ADIPS criteria, gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic thresholds on 75g OGTT are: fasting ≥5.3, 1-hour ≥10.6, or 2-hour ≥[___] mmol/L.
cards.context:
Even modest maternal hyperglycaemia raises fetal hyperinsulinaemia, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycaemia, and shoulder dystocia risk.

ADIPS 2025 replaced the 2014 values (5.1 / 10.0 / 8.5); NSW Health notified services in August 2025, so older questions may differ.

cards.front: In IUGR, absent or reversed end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery Doppler indicates severe [___] and warrants considering delivery.
cards.context:
Umbilical artery Doppler progression in placental insufficiency: normal → raised resistance with elevated S/D ratio → absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) → reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF).

Combine with downstream Dopplers: MCA PSV may show brain-sparing (vasodilation prioritising cerebral perfusion); DV a-wave reversal indicates failing RV function (late ominous sign).

After 32 weeks, AEDF/REDF generally warrants delivery.

cards.front: Emergency contraception: levonorgestrel (LNG, up to [___]h), ulipristal (up to 120h), copper IUD (most effective, up to 5 days). LNG is less effective if BMI >26.
cards.context:
Three EC options with different efficacy and time windows: LNG 1.5 mg PO up to 72 h after UPSI (less effective if BMI >26).

Ulipristal 30 mg PO up to 120 h (more effective than LNG in the 72-120 h window); copper IUD most effective, up to 5 days.

Choice depends on time elapsed, BMI, breastfeeding, preference; consider advance LNG prescription for high-risk patients (perimenopausal, irregular cycles, frequent missed pills).

cards.front: Complete molar pregnancy is karyotype 46,XX (paternal/androgenetic); partial mole is 69,XXY; ~[___]% of complete moles progress to GTN.
cards.context:
Complete mole: empty ovum + sperm that duplicates (46,XX paternal) or two sperm (46,XY paternal) — no fetal tissue, diffuse villous oedema, very high βhCG, 15-20% progress to GTN.

Partial mole: normal ovum + two sperm — triploid, most commonly 69,XXY (dispermic fertilisation of an X-bearing ovum.

69,XXX and 69,XYY occur less often) — abnormal fetal tissue, focal villous oedema, moderate βhCG, ~1-5% malignant risk.

cards.front: PPH is blood loss ≥500 mL after vaginal birth (≥1000 mL after CS); primary = within [___] hours of birth, secondary = beyond that up to 6 weeks postpartum.
cards.context:
The 500 mL threshold for vaginal birth (1000 mL after CS) is a clinical convention, not a physiological cutoff — most women tolerate 500 mL without compromise because of the pregnancy-induced 50% rise in blood volume.

Temporal split: PRIMARY PPH within 24 h (most within 1 h, dominant cause uterine atony — apply 4 Ts); SECONDARY PPH from 24 h to 6 weeks (most in 2nd week, dominant causes retained products and endometritis).

cards.front: Secondary PPH (24 hours to 6 weeks postpartum) is most commonly due to retained products of conception or endometritis; investigate with pelvic [___].
cards.context:
Secondary PPH (24 h to 6 weeks postpartum) has different commonest causes than primary PPH (atony in the first hour).

Workup: pelvic USS for retained products (echogenic intracavity material), FBC for anaemia, βhCG to exclude gestational trophoblastic disease (persistent/rising βhCG → urgent gynae oncology).

cards.front: Erb's palsy is a C5-C6 brachial plexus injury producing 'waiter's tip' — arm adducted, [___] rotated, elbow extended, wrist flexed.
cards.context:
Erb's palsy = upper trunk (C5-C6) brachial plexus injury, classically from excessive lateral head traction during difficult delivery (often after shoulder dystocia).

Deficit map: C5-C6 supplies deltoid, biceps, brachialis, supinator, supraspinatus, infraspinatus — arm hangs adducted, internally rotated, elbow extended, forearm pronated, wrist flexed ('waiter's tip').

Klumpke's palsy (C8-T1) is the lower-trunk injury → 'claw hand' with absent grasp.

cards.front: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a [___] test analysing cell-free fetal DNA from 10 weeks; positive results require invasive CVS/amniocentesis confirmation.
cards.context:
NIPT analyses cell-free fetal DNA fragments shed by placental trophoblast into maternal blood. The 10-week floor is when fetal fraction is high enough to call reliably; earlier risks an uninterpretable 'no result'.

It is a SCREENING test, not diagnostic — the DNA is placental, not directly fetal, so a positive can be confined placental mosaicism, a vanishing twin, or maternal mosaicism.

That is why a positive must be confirmed by an invasive karyotype (CVS or amniocentesis) before any irreversible decision.

cards.front: For stress incontinence, first-line conservative management is supervised pelvic floor muscle training for at least [___] months before reassessment.
cards.context:
PFMT is first-line conservative therapy for stress urinary incontinence; bladder training leads for pure urge/urgency incontinence, with PFMT as an adjunct.

In SUI, stronger levator ani support lifts the bladder neck and improves urethral closure during exertion.

Supervised PFMT needs at least 3 months for strength gains; 60-70% of women improve enough to avoid drug adverse effects or surgery.
